title: Automated data foundation for a live pilot
problem: All findings above are demonstrated on synthetic data and must be re-estimated on Prairie Pulse E-Bikes' real data.
evidence: Public storefront data (prices/specs) are already machine-readable. Internal POS, service and inventory exports are needed.
action: Read-only daily extracts from Prairie Pulse E-Bikes' existing POS/e-commerce and service systems into the same SQLite/warehouse model; add a lost-sale/waitlist capture field.
impact: Enables every recommendation to be measured; no replacement of existing systems.
data: Read-only exports/API access to existing systems

title: Seasonal reorder points and safety stock for A/B-class e-bikes
problem: A flat, non-seasonal reorder rule under-stocks e-bikes in April-June and leaves excess in autumn.
evidence: 14% of e-bike demand unmet; $128,835 gross profit lost to stockouts (TTM). Out-of-sample replay (Jan-Sep 2026): lost GP $126,343 -> $8,877 with a balanced seasonal policy; total policy cost $211,203 -> $108,357.
action: Adopt peak (Apr-Aug) and off-peak reorder points per SKU from Model 4; review weekly; start with the 39 A-class SKUs.
impact: Illustrative: ~$102,846 lower combined stockout + holding + ordering cost over 9 months, requiring ~$152,556 more average inventory in peak.
data: SKU-level daily sales, on-hand, open POs, supplier lead times, waitlist/lost-sale log
kpis: Fill rate, lost-sale units, weeks of cover, inventory turnover, GMROI

title: Forecast-driven pre-season purchase plan by brand and model
problem: Pre-season bulk orders are judgement-based; errors become spring stockouts or autumn clearance.
evidence: Prophet forecast beats seasonal naive by 24% (WAPE) on e-bike units; 12-month unconstrained demand 1,107 units vs 890 forecast sales.
action: Use the quarterly purchase plan (Model 2) as the starting point for Q4/Q1 supplier commitments; refresh monthly.
impact: Q4-2026 recommended e-bike purchases: 136 units; reduces both stockouts and end-of-season markdowns (illustrative).
data: 2+ years of sales, lost-sale estimates, supplier calendars and MOQs

title: 'Ride-ready' accessory bundle and attach-rate target
problem: Accessories earn ~48% margin but are attached to too few bike sales.
evidence: Only 65% of e-bike transactions include an accessory; accessory GP per attached basket $63.
action: Standard bundle (helmet + lock + lights/fenders) offered at every bike sale; attach-rate target 80%; include in sales-expert scorecards.
impact: Illustrative: raising attach to 80% adds ~$8,035 gross profit per year at TTM bike volume.
data: Line-level POS data by sales expert
kpis: Attach rate, accessory $ per bike sale, GM %

title: Protect peak-season workshop capacity
problem: New-bike assembly competes with repairs; turnaround and satisfaction deteriorate in June-July.
evidence: Utilisation peaks at 123% of technician capacity; turnaround 4.5 -> 10.8 days; satisfaction 4.51 -> 3.64.
action: Pre-assemble forecast spring inventory in Feb-Mar, reserve daily repair slots, add a seasonal technician Apr-Aug, triage quick jobs same-day.
impact: Shorter peak turnaround protects ~61%-margin service revenue and online reviews; in the synthetic data, peak turnaround roughly halved in 2026 after seasonal technician capacity was added.
data: Work-order timestamps, technician schedules, assembly log
kpis: Turnaround days, % on-time vs promise, CSAT, utilisation

title: Pre-paid service plans and off-season service campaign
problem: Service is the highest-margin stream but is seasonal and under-penetrated among bike buyers.
evidence: Service gross margin 61%; 67% of bike buyers have used service; winter utilisation ~40-70%. Sensitivity: +15% service revenue = $64,515 operating profit.
action: Sell an annual plan (2 tune-ups + battery check) at bike checkout; run Jan-Mar 'winter tune-up' slots building on the existing 7-point tune-up ($99.99).
impact: Illustrative: $64,515/year operating profit if service revenue grows 15%.
data: Service orders linked to customers and bikes
kpis: Plan attach rate, service revenue/month, off-peak utilisation

title: Test-ride conversion programme
problem: Most leads never book a test ride, although test rides are strongly associated with purchase.
evidence: Conversion 39% with a test ride vs 7% without (association). Free test rides and fitting are part of the store's offer.. Sensitivity: +20% qualified-lead conversion = $82,570 OP.
action: Online test-ride booking prompts on every product page and ad; same-week follow-up; Saturday test-ride events.
impact: Illustrative: up to $82,570/year operating profit if qualified-lead conversion improves 20% (requires inventory and workshop capacity).
data: CRM/lead source, booking system, POS customer match
kpis: Test-ride booking rate, lead-to-sale %, days to convert

title: Discount governance for discretionary e-bike discounts
problem: Non-promotional discounts erode margin without clear volume benefit.
evidence: $78,805 discretionary bike discounts over 33 months ($26,030 TTM); margin falls from ~29% at list to ~21% at the deepest band.
action: Require manager approval above 5%; offer value-adds (accessory credit, free first service) instead of price; track discount by sales expert.
impact: Illustrative: halving discretionary discounts adds ~$13,015 GP/year.
data: Discount reason codes on POS lines
kpis: Average discount %, GM % by sales expert

title: Redesign promotions: keep the spring launch, target clearance
problem: Broad clearance discounts appear to give away margin; spring events appear to create real lift.
evidence: Estimated incremental bike GP: Spring Kick-off $41,842 across 3 years; End-of-Season Clearance -$27,956 (before/after method - indicative).
action: Restrict clearance to SKUs with >6 months cover; test promotions with holdout brands/weeks to measure true incrementality.
impact: Improves promotional ROI; quantifies true lift before scaling (illustrative).
kpis: Incremental GP per promo $, sell-through of targeted SKUs

title: Re-allocate marketing spend using cost per converted customer
problem: Channel budgets are not linked to converted customers or gross profit.
evidence: Cost per conversion ranges from $104 (Email/Newsletter) to $200 (Social Media); average GP per bike sale $772; e-bike customer CLV ~$1,161 GP.
action: Shift 15-20% of the highest-CPA budget to the lowest-CPA channels and referral rewards; implement UTM + POS matching for attribution.
impact: Same spend, more converted customers (illustrative); proper attribution prevents cutting channels that assist conversions.
data: Ad platform spend, UTM/lead source, POS customer match
kpis: Cost per lead, cost per sale, ROAS on GP

title: Winter cost and revenue plan
problem: Fixed costs exceed winter contribution, so the store loses money in roughly half the months.
evidence: Break-even ~$252,623/month at a 31.8% contribution margin; 17 of 33 months loss-making; margin of safety 4%.
action: Flex rosters Nov-Feb, concentrate ads on spring pre-orders, run winter service/storage packages, offer pre-season deposits for spring delivery.
impact: Smaller winter losses and better cash flow (illustrative).
data: Monthly P&L by line, roster hours
kpis: Monthly operating profit, labour % of revenue, pre-order deposits

title: Assortment rationalisation and special-order model for slow brands
problem: Long-tail models tie up capital and floor space.
evidence: Bottom 10 of 56 models = 6.7% of bike revenue; 8 SKUs hold >6 months cover ($98,123 at cost); several premium/cargo brands turn <2x/year.
action: Floor one demo unit for low-turn premium/cargo models and sell via special order; redeploy capital to A-class SKUs.
impact: Illustrative: release part of $98,123 working capital and reduce carrying cost ($71,544 TTM).
data: SKU turnover, margin, supplier special-order lead times
kpis: Turnover by brand, GMROI, aged stock $

title: Customer lifecycle CRM by segment
problem: Customers are not systematically developed after the first purchase.
evidence: 1,222 'New E-Bike Buyers' and 2,718 'Lapsed Service-only Customers'; repeat rate 25%; CLV ~$1,161 GP.
action: Automated journeys: onboarding (30-day check, accessory offer), 3-month service reminder, spring win-back, upgrade/trade-in at 24-30 months.
impact: Higher service and accessory frequency among existing owners at low marginal cost (illustrative).
data: Customer IDs on POS and service orders, email consent
kpis: Repeat rate, service visits per owner, email-attributed revenue
